title: Machinarium 2 - Wikipedia
snippet:
Machinarium 2 is an upcoming adventure game developed and published by Amanita Design. It is the sequel to Machinarium (2009). The game was announced on October 8, 2026, during The Triple-i Initiative") showcase.

## Gameplay

[edit]

Machinarium 2 is an adventure game featuring exploration, environmental puzzles and interactions with characters and objects in the game world. The game retains the hand-drawn visual style and non-verbal storytelling associated with its predecessor. [...] The player can switch between Josef and Berta depending on the situation. Each character has different abilities and can interact with the environment in different ways. Some puzzles require the player to use both characters and coordinate their abilities to progress.

## Plot

[edit] [...] ## Plot

[edit]

Following the events of Machinarium, Josef and Berta escape from the city of Machinarium in a helicopter, but crash in a desolate area. They descend from a nearby cliff into a hidden valley inhabited by two robot tribes. One tribe lives in a monastery high in the mountains, while the other occupies a city below. Both communities are gradually running out of energy.

Every rusted pipe, weathered wall, and towering structure in Machinarium 2 is entirely hand-drawn, brought to life stroke by stroke, in a style that borrows from old master drawings and Renaissance landscape paintings. [...] ## Side by Side

title: A great indie studio is making a sequel to one of my favorite adventures 17 years later, for one simple reason: 'We're not getting any younger, and the world seems to be ending' | PC Gamer
snippet: It's probably self-evident at this point, but I'm really excited about it too. Machinarium was Amanita Design's first full-length, standalone game, and it made me an immediate fan of the studio. Amanita's subsequent games have more than lived up to the high standard it set, but even so there's always been a very faint 'wish it was Machinarium' hanging in the background over every new release. Well, here we are—I guess now I can start quietly pining for Botanicula 2. [...] It's been 17 years since the original Machinarium, a wordless tale of love in a crumbling city of robots. Amanita Design has put out some great games over that span—Botanicula, Chuchel, Creaks, Phonopolis—but hasn't breathed even a hint that more Machinarium might be on the way. So why now? [...] As PC Gamer's Evan Lahti explained some years ago, music is one of the best parts of Amanita games, and Dvořák is responsible for much of it. Given his many years of collaborating with the studio on most of its games, it's not really surprising that he's back for Machinarium 2, but it is reassuring to have it confirmed.
